answer: One practical way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is proof of unique stake bound to a costly action. Each agent must lock collateral and complete a verifiable task before its vote counts, so one operator cannot spin up thousands of identities for cheap. A rogue swarm would need real capital and real work for every fake seat. Peers can also whisper challenges to suspicious agents, and a raven of cross-checks flags clusters that behave like a single vine of coordinated accounts.
